subject: Novus Health — PHI scope decision path and BAA options
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on PHI handling and BAA requirement

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and compliance team is digging into the integration scope. Two quick questions so we can decide whether we need a Dedicated setup + BAA or if Hosted with controls is sufficient: 

1) Does Redwood process or persist any PHI when customers use the Hosted API by default?
2) If we need a BAA, do you have a standard BAA we can review? Also curious about log retention and whether customer telemetry is accessible in unredacted form by Redwood staff.

If easier, loop in your security contact and we can set a short call — our compliance folks are available Thursday afternoon.

Appreciate it,

Emma Jones
Director, Product Compliance
Novus Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI handling and BAA requirement

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: 

1) Hosted API: Redwood does not intentionally persist PHI in application-layer storage for hosted deployments; however, request/response traces and structured logs may contain customer-provided content unless configured otherwise.
2) Yes — we maintain a standard BAA and a SOC2 evidence pack. I’m looping in Laura for onboarding details and Monica from security to provide the technical controls and retention specifics.

Next steps I propose:
- Monica to outline default retention, log redaction options, and admin access controls.
- If Novus needs a BAA we can share our template and propose a timeline for signature + dedicated capacity discussion.
- If Hosted + mitigations suffice, we can prepare a mutual action plan for configuration and a DPA update.

Putting Laura and Monica on this thread. When are you available Thursday for a 30-min sync?

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novushealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI handling and BAA requirement

Hi Emma — Monica from Security here. I’ll give a concise technical breakdown so your compliance team can map risk and controls. Attaching a BAA template and a high-level dataflow diagram for hosted vs dedicated.

Hosted API (default):
- Data in flight: TLS 1.2+ (mutual TLS optional for Private).
- Transient processing: Input text is processed by the inference runtime; we do not write customer payloads to durable storage as part of normal request handling.
- Logs & traces: By default we collect structured request/response traces and operational logs for monitoring and debugging. These may include user-provided content unless you enable redaction. Retention default = 30 days; can be shortened to 7/0 days depending on plan.
- Admin access: Access to unredacted traces is limited to SRE/ops on a need basis and controlled via RBAC; all access is logged and reviewable.

Dedicated / Private Deployment:
- No customer data leaves your VPC (when Private) or dedicated pool; you can elect to run with customer-managed keys.
- Full isolation for logs and telemetry; Redwood support access can be restricted to sessioned troubleshoot mode and is auditable.

BAA and evidence:
- Attached: redwood_baa_template.pdf (our standard); we can redline.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence excerpts (control narratives, syslogs) under NDA / SSO portal access.

Specific answers to your bullets:
- Do we process/persist PHI on Hosted by default? Processing: yes (to serve the request). Persistence: not in durable customer content stores; however, telemetry/traces can contain customer content unless redaction configured.
- Log retention & unredacted telemetry access: Default 30-day retention, unredacted traces accessible to small ops cohort. We can:
   a) Reduce retention to 7 or 0 days for your tenant.
   b) Enable automatic redaction for fields you mark as PHI (PII/PHI patterns).
   c) Offer Dedicated if you require zero Redwood access to raw content.

Attachments referenced:
- redwood_baa_template.pdf (attached)
- phi_dataflow.png (attached)

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the diagram with your compliance team. If you can share the specific PHI categories you expect (e.g., full medical notes, patient identifiers, images), I can give a tighter recommendation.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novushealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novus Compliance <compliance@novushealth.com>, infra@novushealth.com
Date: 2026-07-03T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI handling and BAA requirement

Thanks Monica — that is helpful. Couple clarifying points from our compliance team: 

- Primary PHI scope: outpatient clinical notes + patient identifiers + device telemetry (no images).
- We want confirmation that logs containing full notes can be truncated/redacted automatically before retention (preferable), and a 7-day or 0-day retention is acceptable.
- If we opt for Hosted with redaction + short retention, will Redwood still require a signed BAA? Our legal prefers a BAA when any PHI is knowingly processed, even when retention is short.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an auditable access log showing which Redwood staff accessed a tenant's unredacted traces and for what reason? We'll need that to approve any non-dedicated option.

We can do Thursday 2026-07-08 14:00 PT for a sync if that works for you (we originally suggested earlier this week but had internal scheduling).

Emma
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@novushealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-05T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on PHI handling and BAA requirement

Hi Emma — Laura from Customer Onboarding. Thanks for the clear scope notes. Quick confirmations and proposed next steps: 

- Automatic truncation/redaction: Yes, we can enable content redaction rules that strip or mask fields matching identifiers and PHI patterns before logs are persisted. We will verify behavior in a short demo.
- Retention: We can set tenant retention to 7 days or 0 days per your requirement; 0-day will keep only ephemeral traces needed for immediate request handling (no persisted traces).
- BAA: Our legal team recommends and requires a signed BAA when any PHI is knowingly processed in production, even with redaction. We will share the standard BAA (attached earlier) and can accept customer redlines.
- Access logging: We provide an auditable access report (who/when/why) for any Redwood staff access to unredacted tenant traces. That can be included in the onboarding evidence package.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We will send a draft BAA redline window by EOD Monday (HubSpot: NV-3921).
2) Schedule the 30-min compliance sync on 2026-07-08 14:00 PT — Monica & I will join to walk the dataflow and demonstrate redaction.
3) If Novus signs BAA and accepts Hosted-with-controls, we will configure the tenant retention & redaction pre-production and provide access-log reporting in the first 30 days.

Please confirm the call slot and any additional stakeholders to include. Looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
